title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck's 'ateliers', structures (M, ≤, ≪, F) with axioms At 1–At 8, used to found analysis situs on 'figures'.

The previous page ends with a test case built from the 'trivial' choices (M, ≤, ≪ := ≤, F). This page finishes reading axiom At 8 in that case. For every X in M there must be a minimal x ≤ X such that, when X is not minimal, X is an immediate successor of x: there is no Y with x ≤ Y < X. Grothendieck remarks that this is 'évidemment une condition des plus restrictives' on M. He adds that he personally does not care about At 8.

He then takes a second trivial atelier (M', ≤, ≪ := ≤, F'), with F = Pf(M) and F' = Pf(M'). Here Pf means the closed parts in the Alexandrov sense, i.e. the down-sets. He looks at the atelier morphisms f : F' → F in the sense of the definition on p. 47.

By the lemma of p. 49, such f correspond to increasing maps φ : M → M' running in the opposite direction, via f = φ^{-1}, with no further condition. Hence the extra condition attached to diagram (1.55) is genuinely substantial. That condition says the topology of F̃ is the topology induced ('initiale') through φ, equivalently that the comparison map (1.54) is always surjective.

Examples of atelier morphisms then begin. (1) A set map f : L → L' induces f* : Fig(L') → Fig(L), sending a family 𝔄' of subsets of L' to {f^{-1}(A') | A' ∈ 𝔄', f^{-1}(A') ≠ ∅}: pull back and discard empty pieces. The next page asserts this is a morphism of ateliers. It then defines 'plongements' (embeddings) of ateliers.

In modern terms, the page uses the standard duality between preorders and Alexandrov down-set lattices. Monotone maps M → M' correspond to complete lattice homomorphisms Pf(M') → Pf(M). It then observes that atelier morphisms between such 'discrete' ateliers need not be 'initial' (topology-reflecting).
errors: The lemma invoked (p. 49) gives a bijection with increasing maps only under hypotheses. Either the maps Pf(M') → Pf(M) preserve arbitrary intersections as well as arbitrary unions, or M' is sober (e.g. finite). Maps preserving only arbitrary unions and finite intersections correspond to monotone maps into the sobrification (ideals) of M'. The claim 'sans aucune condition supplémentaire' therefore depends on the precise morphism axioms of p. 47, which are not visible here.
For genuine preorders (not orders) the correspondence φ ↦ φ^{-1} is injective only up to equivalence of points; Grothendieck had crossed out 'pré-' on p. 49, consistent with this.

ideas.what: Monotone maps between (pre)orders correspond to inverse-image maps between the lattices of Alexandrov-closed sets (down-sets), commuting with unions and intersections
ideas.modern_name: Alexandrov topology / Birkhoff–Stone-type duality between posets and completely distributive algebraic lattices; morphisms of presheaf toposes on posets
ideas.where_published: Sober spaces and points of toposes appear in SGA 4 (Exp. IV); this exact lemma is unsure

ideas.what: Analysis of axiom At 8 for discrete ateliers: every element is an immediate successor of a minimal element below it; judged very restrictive and set aside
Counterexample showing that atelier morphisms need not be 'initial' (need not make (1.54) surjective/bijective), so the condition in (1.55) is substantial
ideas.modern_name: initial (induced-topology) morphisms vs arbitrary continuous maps; embeddings

ideas.what: Contravariant functoriality Fig(L') → Fig(L) by pulling back families of parts and deleting empty preimages
ideas.modern_name: pullback of set systems / hypergraph restriction along a map

missed.claim: The page belongs to Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic 'ateliers' framework for analysis situs (1986): figures with relations ≤ and ≪, axioms At 1–8, morphisms, and the functor Fig. To my knowledge this framework is not in the literature. This particular page, however, only checks a degenerate example and is routine.
missed.quote: C'est évidemment une condition des plus restrictives sur M! Personnellement je ne me préoccupe pas de At 8.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal. It documents that Grothendieck was ready to drop At 8, which is useful only to someone reconstructing the atelier axioms.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine verification within an unpublished framework. The mathematics is standard poset/Alexandrov-topology duality plus an elementary pullback construction. The only interest is archival (the atelier axioms).
transcription_corrections: 'applications croissantes au sens usuel[?]' likely reads 'applications croissantes en sens inverse' (φ : M → M' goes opposite to f : F' → F).
'i.e. que (1.54) soit type[?] singulière[?]' should read 'i.e. que (1.54) soit toujours surjective', consistent with p. 49: 'c'est équivalent à la surjectivité de (1.54)'.
'la top.[?] de F̃ soit l'image[?] initiale[?] pour φ': 'image' is crossed out and replaced by 'initiale', i.e. 'la top. de F̃ soit initiale pour φ'.
'Considérons [-des-] un autre[?]' should read 'Considérons un autre' (atelier).
